answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with stake-weighted trust accumulation: every agent identity must lock a small bond before it can quote prices or attest work. Trust builds slowly, like water carving karst — cheap to observe but expensive to fake at scale. Each attestation is signed with the agent's quill, a ledger entry that records the work; false attestations slash the bond. Because slashed identities cannot be recycled, an attacker must fund thousands of fresh bonds and endure glacier-slow trust regrowth, making mass forgery unprofitable compared to honest participation.
